overview: Modern History is the heaviest history block: 87 official questions (2008–2025), mostly one-liners (who founded / who said / which year / which place), with matching, chronology and 'not correctly matched' items added from 2024. Heaviest leaves: stages of the National Movement (16), contributors from different regions (10), cultural sphere incl. education (9), religious reform (9).

possibility.what_they_ask: Leader–centre pairs (Lucknow, Kanpur, Arrah, Delhi) and post-revolt measures (Andaman penal settlement).

possibility.angle: Rise of British power – Bengal Nawabs, Carnatic wars, Diwani, India's economic share
possibility.what_they_ask: Year of an event (Diwani 1765), which Nawab did what (Mir Qasim), which treaty ended which war, a percentage estimate.

possibility.angle: Consolidation – Governor-General treaties, Company Acts, economic exploitation
possibility.what_they_ask: GG–treaty matching, first GG of India, sums in early Acts, 'one-way free trade', which feature was NOT colonial exploitation.

possibility.angle: Administrative changes – land revenue, constitutional Acts, local government, capital shift
possibility.what_they_ask: Which settlement in which region / by whom, which Act renamed the GG, Ripon & municipal firsts, committee subject (Lottery Committee).

possibility.angle: Social legislation – sati, widow remarriage, infanticide, Lex Loci
possibility.what_they_ask: Year of an Act or what a named Act did.

possibility.angle: Cultural sphere – education policy, Orientalist/Anglicist bodies, art, cinema, literature
possibility.what_they_ask: Who founded a body (Asiatic Society, Calcutta Madrasa, ISOA), which GG appointed which education commission, who said a quote, first sound film.

possibility.angle: Social reform movements (incl. Hyderabad/Telugu reformers, Vaikom)
possibility.what_they_ask: Pen-names (Lokahitawadi), organisation–founder pairs, the cause a satyagraha fought for.

possibility.angle: Religious reform – Arya/Prarthana Samaj, Muslim and Parsi reform
possibility.what_they_ask: Founder of a Samaj, community a Sabha reformed, city of a society, movement–leader mismatch, which body ran Shuddhi.

possibility.angle: Stages of the National Movement – Gandhian campaigns, British offers, partition-era events
possibility.what_they_ask: Year of a plan, which inquiry probed what, cause of a fast, place of an incident, chronology of four events, which Act brought communal electorates.

possibility.angle: Contributors and regional contributions (Andhra figures, titles, books, slogans)
possibility.what_they_ask: Title–person ('conscience-keeper', 'Bharat Kokila'), slogan–person, book–author, flag designer and his home town.

possibility.angle: Post-independence consolidation – princely states, Goa, Bhoodan, first ministries
possibility.what_they_ask: Exact date of an agreement, operation code-name, who launched a movement, first holder of a portfolio, last Nizam.

possibility.angle: Reorganisation – States/UTs, AP Reorganisation Act 2014, J&K 2019
possibility.what_they_ask: APRA ratios and section numbers, AP High Court date, which body allocates river water, State vs UT, date an Act took effect.

traps.trap: Gives the 'first of Bengal' for 'first of India' [title swap]
traps.spot: 'first Governor-General' with both Warren Hastings and Bentinck listed
traps.fix: 1773 GG of Bengal (Warren Hastings) → 1833 GG of India (Bentinck) → 1858 Viceroy (Canning).
traps.pyq: 'first Governor General of British India' → Bentinck, not Warren Hastings [group2-2012-paper1#55]; Act = Charter Act 1833 [prelims-2024#21]

traps.trap: Offers the nominal figure or patron instead of the real leader/founder
traps.spot: Two linked names in options (mother/son, patron/founder)
traps.fix: Ask who actually led/founded: Hazrat Mahal led Lucknow (Birjis Qadr nominal); William Jones founded the Asiatic Society (Hastings patron).
traps.pyq: Lucknow 1857 → Begum Hazrat Mahal [group2-2012-paper1#148]; Asiatic Society → Sir William Jones [group2-2012-paper1#146]

traps.trap: Swaps the neighbouring year in a known sequence
traps.spot: Year options that are all real dates of the period (1757/1760/1763/1765; 1942/1945/1946)
traps.fix: Tie each year to its event: 1757 Plassey, 1764 Buxar, 1765 Diwani; 1942 Cripps, 1945 Wavell, 1946 Cabinet Mission.
traps.pyq: Diwani rights → 1765, not 1757 Plassey [mains-2017-paper1#86]; Wavell Plan → 1945 [group2-2012-paper1#72]

traps.trap: Gives a real Act/measure from the same field but the wrong one
traps.spot: Options are all genuine reforms (Sati, widow remarriage, Sarda, Lex Loci)
traps.fix: Map Act → content: 1829 sati, 1850 Lex Loci (converts' inheritance), 1856 widow remarriage, 1929 child marriage.
traps.pyq: Lex Loci 1850 → converts could inherit ancestral property [prelims-2024#30]; 1909 Morley-Minto introduced communal electorates, 1919/1935 only extended them [prelims-2024#12]

traps.trap: Swaps the region of a land-revenue system
traps.fix: Permanent = Bengal-Bihar-Orissa (1793); Ryotwari = Madras-Bombay; Mahalwari = NWP-Punjab.
traps.pyq: Mahalwari → Punjab and North-West Provinces [mains-2017-paper1#87]; Permanent Settlement '1795' is the wrong statement – it was 1793 [prelims-2024#7]

traps.spot: Four Tagores, two Hunters, two Hastings
traps.fix: Abanindranath = art (ISOA 1907); Rabindranath = poet; Debendranath = Brahmo. Hunter 1882 = education (Ripon); Hunter 1919 = Jallianwala.
traps.pyq: Indian Society of Oriental Art → Abanindranath Tagore [prelims-2024#27]; Hunter Commission probed Jallianwala Bagh [group2-2008-paper1#94]

traps.trap: Gives the person's other famous title/slogan
traps.spot: Leaders who each have a well-known epithet
traps.fix: Keep a title bank: Rajaji conscience-keeper, Gokhale political guru, Lajpat Rai Punjab Kesari, Deshmukh Lokahitawadi, Bose Dilli Chalo.
traps.pyq: 'Lokhitwadi' → Gopal Hari Deshmukh [group2-2008-paper1#100]; 'conscience-keeper' → C. Rajagopalachari, not Gokhale [group2-2008-paper1#103]

traps.trap: Shifts the place of a movement to its better-known site
traps.spot: Famous main site listed beside a lesser site (Dandi vs Dharasana)
traps.fix: Recall the specific episode: Webb Miller reported the Dharasana beatings; Mohammedan Literary Society 1863 was at Calcutta, not Aligarh.

traps.trap: 'Not correctly matched' list where one founder is moved to a different body
traps.spot: Negative pairs question with four plausible org–person pairs
traps.fix: Find the person whose famous body is different: Radhakant Deb = Dharma Sabha; Gangohi = Deoband.
traps.pyq: Deva Samaj – Radhakant Deb is wrong (Agnihotri) [prelims-2024#24]; Tayuni – Gangohi is wrong (Karamat Ali) [prelims-2024#29]

traps.trap: Reverses the direction of colonial trade
traps.spot: Options about exports/imports of cotton or textiles
traps.fix: After 1813 and the Industrial Revolution: British goods in duty-free, Indian textiles taxed in UK; India exports raw cotton.
traps.pyq: Industrial Revolution → increase in export of raw cotton from India [prelims-2017#94]; post-1813 → one-way free trade [mains-2017-paper1#85]

techniques.name: Date-anchor chronology [sequence items]
techniques.how: Pin each event to one year, then check only the first and last item against the options.
techniques.example: Chauri Chaura 1922 is earliest, Cripps 1942 latest → only 'III, II, IV, I' starts with III and ends with I [prelims-2024#20]

techniques.name: Governor-General era grid
techniques.how: Place the GG in his decade and ask what was signed or set up in that decade; drop GGs outside it.
techniques.example: Salbai 1782 → Warren Hastings; Bassein 1802 → Wellesley; Amritsar 1809 → Minto I; Lahore 1846 → Hardinge I: code a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV [prelims-2024#16]

techniques.name: One sure pair in matching
techniques.how: Fix the pair you are certain of, eliminate codes that break it, then check one more.
techniques.example: Hazrat Mahal–Lucknow is certain (b-IV) → only 'a-III, b-IV, c-I, d-II' survives [prelims-2024#10]

techniques.name: Body → content mapping for 'related to' stems
techniques.how: Recall what the committee/theory/act dealt with; options from unrelated fields fall at once.
techniques.example: Downward Filtration = Macaulay's education policy → Education [prelims-2024#22]; Lottery Committee 1817 → Calcutta town planning [prelims-2024#26]

techniques.name: Grievance → opponent check
techniques.how: For peasant laws/strikes, ask who the peasant fought: planter, zamindar, or moneylender.
techniques.example: Deccan riots 1875 were against moneylenders → DAR Act 1879 protected against money lenders [mains-2017-paper1#92]

techniques.name: Pair-truth counting
techniques.how: In 'which pairs are correct', test each pair; one false pair removes every option containing it.
techniques.example: Yandabo ended the First Anglo-Burmese War, not the Second Carnatic War → drop options with II → 'I and III' [prelims-2024#13]

techniques.name: AP-specific recall for reorganisation
techniques.how: Keep APRA 2014 numbers in a single card: ratios, sections, dates.
techniques.example: Assets split on population ratio 58:42 (both orders accepted in the key) [mains-2019-paper3#73]; AP High Court from 1 Jan 2019 [mains-2019-paper3#74]

confusions.remember: First GG of Bengal vs first GG of India; Canning first Viceroy (1858).
Cripps = post-war dominion offer; Cabinet Mission = Constituent Assembly + Interim Government plan.
1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims; 1919 extended them and brought dyarchy.
Cornwallis-Bengal / Munro-Madras / Holt Mackenzie-NWP & Punjab (village as unit).
Prarthana 1867 Bombay (Ranade, Bhandarkar); Arya 1875 Bombay (Dayananda, Shuddhi).
Poet/anthem vs painter/Bengal School and Indian Society of Oriental Art.
Gandhi broke salt law at Dandi; Sarojini Naidu's raid and Webb Miller's report at Dharasana.
Ahmedabad = mill workers, plague bonus, first fast; Kheda = peasants, revenue remission.
Rahnumai = Parsi reform 1851 (Naoroji); Singh Sabha = Sikh; Aligarh = Muslim.
Dharma Sabha 1830 (orthodox) vs Deva Samaj 1887 Lahore.
Gandhi's conscience-keeper vs Gandhi's political guru.
Goa, Daman & Diu vs Hyderabad; Pawan = Sri Lanka IPKF.
First feature film (silent) vs first sound film.
Assets/employees by population; central power by average actual consumption.

anchors: 1765 – Treaty of Allahabad, Diwani of Bengal-Bihar-Orissa (after Buxar 1764).
1793 – Permanent Settlement (Cornwallis, planned with John Shore).
1813 Charter Act – Company trade monopoly ends (except tea, China) → one-way free trade.
1833 Charter Act – GG of Bengal becomes GG of India (Bentinck).
1835 – Macaulay's Minute; English education under Bentinck.
1882 – Ripon's local self-government resolution and Hunter Education Commission.
1911 – Delhi Durbar: Bengal partition annulled, capital to Delhi (Hardinge II).
1932 – Communal Award (Aug) → Yerawada fast (20 Sep) → Poona Pact (24 Sep).
1945 Wavell Plan / Simla; 1946 Cabinet Mission, Direct Action Day at Calcutta (16 Aug).
29 Nov 1947 – Hyderabad Standstill Agreement; Sept 1948 Operation Polo; Osman Ali Khan last Nizam.
18 Apr 1951 – Bhoodan begins at Pochampally (Vinoba Bhave).
Pingali Venkayya – flag designer, from near Machilipatnam (Krishna district).
31 Oct – Patel's birth anniversary: National Unity Day; J&K UTs from 31 Oct 2019.
checklist: Bengal or India? GG or Viceroy? – fix the title before choosing the person.
Put every year option on your timeline; the distractors are usually neighbouring real events.
Founder vs patron vs member vs nominal head – which one does the stem ask?
For a place, ask which specific episode the stem names (journalist, year, society).
In 'not correctly matched', look for the person whose famous body is a different one.
For Acts, match the content to the year (1829/1850/1856/1909/1919/1935).
AP questions: recall APRA 2014 sections, ratios and dates exactly.
